plans.note: Section 15 is expressly headed 'Limitation of Garman's Liability', so it is likely one-sided; check the cap amount, mutuality, and whether IP indemnity (sec-13) and confidentiality (sec-14) breaches are carved out.

Section 13 is the IP indemnity; assess scope (defence, costs, settlement control, remedies on injunction) and whether any Sparkling-side indemnity is broader than necessary. Cross-check the liability cap in sec-15 does not swallow it.

No non-compete heading appears; if any restraint on Sparkling's business or on buying/building competing routing software exists it would sit in sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) or the general matters clause.
No exclusivity heading; scan the grant, use restrictions and maintenance/fees sections for any sole-source or exclusive-supplier language before concluding absent.
Likely no MFN. If a pricing-favour clause appears in the fees or maintenance sections, confirm direction — only an MFN obliging Sparkling to give Garman best terms is objectionable.
Section 19 is the non-solicitation clause; check mutuality, duration (12 months preferred), employee scope, and whether general advertising/unsolicited applications are carved out.

Section 17 (Term and Termination) is primary; the reject options in sec-7/8 and maintenance cancellation in sec-10 may give Sparkling an exit. Confirm Sparkling can terminate on notice without penalty and that Garman cannot terminate for convenience mid-term.
Maintenance term typically auto-renews annually; check sec-10 and sec-17 for the renewal mechanic, the non-renewal notice window (30-60 days preferred) and any uncapped fee uplift in sec-11.

Governing law, venue and any arbitration provision should sit in the General Matters section; verify the chosen jurisdiction against the accepted list and that courts rather than foreign arbitration apply.
Assignment is normally in General Matters; also check sec-2 for licence transfer limits and sec-17 for any termination right triggered by Sparkling's change of control.

Confirm Garman retains only its pre-existing software IP and claims no ownership of Sparkling's data, configurations or converted data (sec-4) or of feedback/modifications; escrow (sec-16) and confidentiality (sec-14) support our data position.

Section 2 grants the licence and sec-3 restricts use; check that affiliates and contractors/outsourcers at Authorized Locations are covered, that the grant is perpetual/irrevocable once paid, and that 'Authorized Locations' in the definitions/schedules is not unduly narrow.
No audit heading; if a licence-verification or inspection right exists it would be embedded in the use restrictions or general matters — test notice, frequency, on-site access and who bears cost.
Look for late-payment interest, early-termination charges or penalties on Sparkling in the fees and termination sections; service credits or refunds in our favour are not flagged.

Section 12 carries the specifications and warranty; check the warranty period, that conformity is measured against the Specifications, the remedy (repair/replace then refund), and how it interacts with acceptance testing (sec-6) and the reject option (sec-7).

No insurance heading appears; check General Matters before concluding absent. Garman personnel attend Authorized Locations for installation and training, so a standard insurance covenant is warranted.
Check the fees section and any fee schedule for minimum licence counts, committed maintenance years or take-or-pay volumes binding Sparkling.

Section 17 likely requires return/destruction of software on termination but probably no exit assistance or return of Sparkling's data; confirm against sec-18 (survival) and the escrow clause before marking missing.
